conflicts.description: The switch matrix prints Laser Kick; the playfield location/wiring illustrations and retained runtime call the same address Kick Back/Kickback. The combined label preserves both terms.

The manual prints a physical Right E.O.S. switch, while FLIP4746 and the retained script use address 46 as right-flipper button state. The damaged schematic prevents reconciling the physical circuit with the controller-facing behavior.

The manual prints a physical Left E.O.S. switch, while FLIP4746 and the retained script use address 47 as left-flipper button state. The damaged schematic prevents reconciling the physical circuit with the controller-facing behavior.

The printed lamp matrix assigns address 8 to Return to Base. The retained script has no lamp-8 callback and uses its l8a-v tower helpers under solenoid 5 instead, so no physical lamp-8 placement is asserted.

The Coil I.D. Chart prints 2L twice, first for Ramp Multiplier and then for Red Hot Dog. Ramp Multiplier's BLK-BRN/ORN drive shares Q46 with 1L Explosion's VIO-BRN/BRN drive, so it is the 1R relay side and therefore public address 25; the following printed location list independently says 1R, and the retained script corroborates SolCallback(25) as Ramp Multiplier (with 26 Green Shield and 29 Knocker). Public 25 is the documented resolution, while the duplicate printed 2L remains preserved in the excerpt and alias.

Both printed coil lists call Mars Yellow device type COIL: 23-800, while the otherwise matching Mars Red and Mars Blue rows say #89 BULBS. Pinned s11.c independently treats the yellow, red and blue Mars flashers as one two-bulb-per-colour group, so kind flasher is the documented resolution; the printed COIL: 23-800 disagreement is retained verbatim and remains first-class provenance.

mechanisms.behavior: The retained script initializes all three trough switches active. Pulsing the ball-trough eject moves the front ball from switch 12 into the shooter lane; the remaining balls advance toward switch 12.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball closes the outhole switch. The outhole coil kicks that ball into the three-ball trough; the script explicitly clears switch 13 when it fires.
mechanisms.label: Outhole feeder

mechanisms.behavior: The saucer captures one ball, asserts switch 25, and the red-eject coil kicks it back to the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Red eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: The saucer captures one ball, asserts switch 33, and the yellow-eject coil kicks it back to the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Yellow eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: The saucer captures one ball, asserts switch 38, and the blue-eject coil kicks it back to the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Blue eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: The CPU output controls a 24 VDC Laser Kick relay. The retained runtime arms the kickback while that relay is active; a ball crossing switch 17 then receives the local kick. This is relay-gated behavior, not causality inferred from the label.
mechanisms.label: Left outlane kickback

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 15 when the left sling surface fires. The physical special-coil address is unresolved because the decisive schematic region is missing.
mechanisms.label: Left slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 14 when the right sling surface fires. The physical special-coil address is unresolved because the decisive schematic region is missing.
mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 43 on a red pop-bumper hit. The physical special-coil address is unresolved.
mechanisms.label: Red pop bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 44 on a yellow pop-bumper hit. The physical special-coil address is unresolved.
mechanisms.label: Yellow pop bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The retained runtime pulses switch 45 on a blue pop-bumper hit. The physical special-coil address is unresolved.
mechanisms.label: Blue pop bumper

mechanisms.behavior: PinMAME synthesizes lower-left power/hold outputs and the script fires the left flipper callback. The printed EOS label conflicts with the runtime button-state use, and the damaged schematic prevents a complete physical circuit claim.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper

mechanisms.behavior: PinMAME synthesizes lower-right power/hold outputs and the script fires the right flipper callback. The printed EOS label conflicts with the runtime button-state use, and the damaged schematic prevents a complete physical circuit claim.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: A passive spinner pulses switch 27 as it turns; it has no CPU actuator.
mechanisms.label: Red spinner

mechanisms.behavior: A passive spinner pulses switch 51 as it turns; it has no CPU actuator.
mechanisms.label: Yellow spinner

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the ramp closes switch 29 and follows the retained table's wire-ramp path back toward the shooter-side return. No motor or diverter is scripted.
mechanisms.label: Wire ramp and return path

mechanisms.behavior: The spring plunger is player-driven. A launched ball traverses shooter-lane switch 52; there is no physical CPU shooter coil.
mechanisms.label: Manual plunger and shooter lane
